title: Charat Singh’s Marksmanship and the Split of the Caravan

blocks.text: The page opens with praise of Charat Singh's speed and accuracy in battle, showing him firing one loaded musket after another and snatching fresh weapons from nearby comrades without breaking momentum. His marksmanship is remembered as exceptional even among seasoned Sikh fighters.

Amid that struggle, The caravan carried two copies of holy Guru Granth Sahib, a detail that raises the emotional and religious stakes of the retreat. The defenders are not only saving lives but also trying to protect sacred manuscripts while Abdali's troops close in around them.

As the pressure mounts, the Singhs are driven into a harsher fight in which firearms run low and even sticks and stones are used. The page joins admiration for Charat Singh's battlefield skill to the broader tragedy of a caravan being split apart under relentless assault.
